content.title: About
content.content: Chicken nuggets are breaded pieces of chicken breast meat that are deep‑fried or baked. They are a staple of fast‑food menus and are usually served with dipping sauces. Nuggets have a crispy coating and tender meat inside.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first commercial nugget recipe was developed in the 1970s by McDonald’s.
The name “nuggets” comes from the English word “nugget,” meaning a small lump or piece.
While most nuggets are made from processed chicken breast, some versions use whole thigh pieces.
In various countries they are paired with unique sauces such as sweet‑and‑sour or teriyaki.
Since the 2020s, vegetarian and vegan nuggets made from plant protein have entered the market.

items.title: Protein source
items.content: The chicken in nuggets provides high‑quality protein essential for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Chicken supplies niacin, vitamin B6 and B12, which support metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Iron and zinc
items.content: Nuggets can contribute to iron and zinc intake, nutrients important for immune health.

items.title: High fat and calorie content
items.content: Because of the breading and frying, nuggets can be calorie‑dense and contain saturated fats.

items.title: Sodium
items.content: Salt used in the coating and sauces may be a concern for people with hypertension.

items.title: Chicken allergy
items.content: A small number of individuals may experience allergic reactions to chicken.

items.title: Trans fats in some preparations
items.content: Frying in oils high in trans fats increases cardiovascular risk.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Nuggets are typically served hot with sauces such as barbecue, honey‑mustard, or cheese dip. They are easy to eat with hands and can be added to salads, wraps, or used as a protein boost in meals.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cooked nuggets in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. Frozen nuggets keep for 2‑3 months; reheat them to an internal temperature of 75 °C before consumption.

content.title: About
content.content: Lettuce Salad is a mix of fresh lettuce leaves and assorted vegetables (cucumber, bell pepper, radish, spring onion, etc.) without tomatoes, carrots, or dressing. It works well as a light snack or side dish.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The salad is over 90 % water, making it an excellent source of hydration.
Lettuce leaves are rich in vitamin K, essential for blood clotting.
Excluding tomatoes and carrots reduces the amount of lycopene and beta‑carotene, focusing the nutrient profile on leafy greens.
Lettuce Salad is often used as a base for more elaborate restaurant dishes.

items.title: High in vitamin K
items.content: Vitamin K supports blood clotting and bone health.

items.title: Low in calories
items.content: The salad provides very few calories, making it suitable for weight‑management diets.

items.title: Source of folate
items.content: Folate is important for DNA synthesis and is especially beneficial for pregnant women.

items.title: Digestive support
items.content: Fiber from the leaves and vegetables promotes regular bowel movements.

items.title: Antioxidant properties
items.content: Contains polyphenols and vitamin C, which help combat free radicals.

items.title: Bacterial contamination
items.content: Raw vegetables can harbor Salmonella or E. coli; thorough washing is essential.

items.title: Leafy‑green allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to certain lettuce varieties.

items.title: Digestive discomfort from excess fiber
items.content: Large portions may cause gas or bloating.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the lettuce salad immediately after preparation to keep the leaves crisp. Add nuts, seeds, or a lean protein such as chicken, turkey, or tofu for extra substance.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the prepared salad in an airtight container in the refrigerator for no more than 24 hours. Keep the vegetables dry to prevent the leaves from becoming soggy.

content.title: About
content.content: Frozen melon consists of ripe melon pieces that are flash‑frozen shortly after harvest to lock in fresh flavor, aroma, and nutrients. It is convenient for smoothies, desserts, sauces, or as a refreshing snack.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Melon belongs to the Cucurbitaceae family, closely related to watermelon and zucchini.
IQF (individually quick frozen) technology keeps the pieces separate and prevents clumping.
Frozen melon is widely used by chefs to create summer‑style dishes year‑round.
Melon is a good source of vitamin C, and proper freezing helps retain most of it.
It is rich in beta‑carotene, which the body converts to vitamin A.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C supports the immune system and aids collagen synthesis.

items.title: Contains beta‑carotene
items.content: Beta‑carotene provides antioxidant protection and promotes eye health.

items.title: Low‑calorie fruit
items.content: Melon is low in calories, making it a suitable option for weight management.

items.title: Hydration
items.content: With over 90 % water content, it helps maintain the body’s fluid balance.

items.title: Potassium
items.content: Potassium supports normal heart and muscle function.

items.title: Cucurbit allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to melons and other cucurbit family members.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Melon contains natural sugars; people with diabetes should monitor portion size.

items.title: Freezing quality
items.content: Improper storage can cause ice crystal formation and degrade flavor.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Add frozen melon to smoothies, fruit cocktails, ice cream, yogurt, make sauces, desserts, or simply thaw and enjoy as a cool snack.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep in a freezer at –18 °C (0 °F) or lower in an airtight bag. Once thawed, consume within 1–2 days and do not refreeze.

content.title: About
content.content: Mixed nuts without peanuts is a blend of selected nuts (almonds, cashews, hazelnuts, walnuts, pine nuts, etc.) lightly salted. The product contains no peanuts, making it safe for people with peanut allergy. The nuts retain their natural aroma and crunchy texture, while a hint of salt enhances their flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Nut mixes are often used in cooking to add texture and flavor to dishes.
The absence of peanuts makes the blend suitable for most diets, including gluten‑free and dairy‑free.
The salt used is usually sea salt, adding trace minerals such as magnesium and iodine.
Nuts in the mix may be roasted separately before being combined to preserve their individual taste notes.
Mixed nuts are a popular snack paired with wine or beer.

items.title: Rich in healthy fats
items.content: Nuts contain monounsaturated and polyunsaturated fatty acids that support heart and vascular health.

items.title: Source of plant protein
items.content: The blend provides a substantial amount of protein useful for muscle maintenance and tissue repair.

items.title: Contains vitamin E
items.content: Vitamin E is a powerful antioxidant that protects cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: High in minerals
items.content: Nuts supply magnesium, phosphorus, zinc and iron, important for metabolism and bone health.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Fiber in nuts promotes regular bowel function and a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Tree nut allergy
items.content: Even without peanuts, the mix can trigger reactions in people allergic to any of the included nuts.

items.title: High in calories
items.content: Nuts are calorie‑dense, so portion control is recommended.

items.title: Salt content
items.content: Individuals monitoring sodium intake should consider the amount of added salt.

items.title: Choking hazard
items.content: Whole nuts can pose a choking risk for young children.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The mixed nuts can be enjoyed as a snack, added to salads, yogurts, muesli, baked goods, or used in sauces. For extra aroma, nuts can be briefly toasted in a dry pan.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the mix in an airtight container in a cool, dry, dark place. For longer shelf life, keep it in the refrigerator or freezer to prevent fat oxidation. Discard nuts that smell rancid or have off‑flavors.

content.title: About
content.content: Nutritional Powder Mix, Protein, NFS (5498) is a high‑quality blend of plant and whey proteins enriched with vitamins and minerals. It is designed to support muscle recovery, increase satiety, and provide essential nutrients.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The blend contains whey protein, pea protein, and spirulina extract.
Each serving delivers over 20 g of pure protein.
Fortified with B‑vitamins, vitamin D, and minerals – calcium, magnesium, zinc.
The product is gluten‑free, lactose‑free, and contains no artificial sweeteners.
Packaging is made from recyclable material and is fully recyclable.

items.title: Supports muscle growth
items.content: A rich protein profile promotes muscle protein synthesis after workouts.

items.title: Improves recovery
items.content: Branched‑chain amino acids (BCAA) help reduce muscle fatigue.

items.title: Boosts immunity
items.content: Vitamins C and E, along with zinc, support a healthy immune system.

items.title: Promotes satiety
items.content: High protein and fiber content keep you feeling full longer.

items.title: Supports bone health
items.content: Calcium and vitamin D contribute to stronger bones.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: The product contains whey protein, which may trigger allergic reactions in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Excessive protein intake
items.content: Very high doses can strain the kidneys, especially in people with pre‑existing kidney conditions.

items.title: Artificial flavorings
items.content: Some variants may include flavorings that are not suitable for those with additive sensitivities.

items.title: Medication interactions
items.content: High vitamin D levels can affect the efficacy of certain drugs, such as steroids.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Mix one scoop (≈30 g) of powder with 250‑300 ml of water, milk, or plant‑based beverage. For extra flavor and texture, add fruit, nuts, or oats. Consume preferably post‑workout or as a nutritious snack.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the powder in a cool, dry place in a tightly sealed container. Keep moisture and direct sunlight away. For long‑term storage (over 12 months) consider refrigerating.

pasta-whole-grain-with-cream-sauce-and-a.title: Whole Grain Pasta with Cream Sauce and Vegetables, Ready-to-Heat

content.title: About
content.content: Whole grain pasta with cream sauce and added vegetables is a ready‑to‑heat meal that can be quickly warmed in a microwave or on the stovetop. It contains whole‑grain pasta, a smooth cream sauce, and a mix of carrots, broccoli, sweet pepper and zucchini. The dish is balanced in protein, carbohydrates and fiber, making it a convenient option for busy people who want a tasty and nutritious meal.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Whole grain pasta provides more fiber and B‑vitamins than traditional white pasta.
The cream sauce is made with low‑fat dairy and plant oils, reducing saturated fat content.
Vegetables are flash‑steamed to retain most of their vitamins and minerals.
The product has a shelf life of up to 12 months when stored in a cool, dry place.
Heating takes only 3–5 minutes, ideal for office lunches and travel.

items.title: High in fiber
items.content: Whole grain pasta supplies dietary fiber that supports healthy digestion and promotes satiety.

items.title: Vitamins and minerals
items.content: The vegetable blend adds vitamin C, vitamin A, potassium and folate, important for immunity and metabolism.

items.title: Low added sugar
items.content: The meal contains no added sugars, making it suitable for blood‑glucose management.

items.title: Plant‑based protein source
items.content: Combined whole grain pasta and vegetables provide a moderate amount of plant protein.

items.title: Moderate healthy fats
items.content: The cream sauce includes monounsaturated fats that support heart health.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: The cream sauce contains milk; individuals with lactose intolerance or dairy allergy should choose an alternative.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: The ready sauce may contain added salt; people monitoring sodium intake should check the label.

items.title: Heat safety
items.content: Insufficient heating can leave bacteria; heat the meal to an internal temperature of at least 75 °C.

items.title: Gluten
items.content: The pasta is wheat‑based and contains gluten; not suitable for those with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Heat a portion in the microwave (≈3 minutes) or on the stovetop, stirring until hot. Serve as a standalone meal or with a green salad. Optional toppings include grated Parmesan or fresh herbs.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the package in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, keep it in an airtight container and consume within 5 days. Discard if an off‑odor or discoloration develops.

content.title: About
content.content: Pork cracklings are fried or roasted pieces of pork fat that become crisp and golden. They have a crunchy texture, rich meaty aroma, and a lightly salty taste. Cracklings are enjoyed as a snack, a garnish, or an ingredient in various dishes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Cracklings have long been a staple in Eastern European, Russian, and Balkan cuisines.
In some regions they are called “pork rind” or “fried pork skin”.
They can be prepared plain, salted, or seasoned with paprika, garlic, pepper, and other spices.
During the Soviet era, cracklings were a common bar snack served with beer.
When stored properly, they stay crunchy for several months.

items.title: Source of protein
items.content: Cracklings provide a notable amount of animal protein, essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: They contain thiamine, riboflavin, and niacin, which support energy metabolism.

items.title: Contains beneficial fats
items.content: While most fat is saturated, cracklings also include monounsaturated and polyunsaturated fatty acids.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: They supply zinc, iron, and selenium, important for immune function and antioxidant protection.

items.title: Low in carbohydrates
items.content: Ideal for low‑carb diets as they contain virtually no sugar.

items.title: High saturated fat content
items.content: Excessive intake may raise cholesterol levels.

items.title: Salt
items.content: Salted cracklings can increase blood pressure; people with hypertension should limit consumption.

items.title: Pork allergy
items.content: Some individuals may have an allergic reaction to pork.

items.title: Calorie dense
items.content: Cracklings are very calorie‑rich, so portion control is important.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cracklings can be eaten straight as a snack, added to salads, soups, porridges, or used as a filling for pastries and buns. They are also commonly served alongside beer or kvass. For a less salty option, choose unsalted varieties.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep cracklings in an airtight container in a cool, dry place away from direct light. For longer shelf life, store them in the refrigerator or freezer to prevent the fat from becoming rancid. Discard any that develop a burnt or off‑flavor.

content.title: About
content.content: Fresh mashed potato (NFS) is a ready‑to‑eat product made by boiling and puréeing selected fresh potatoes without any preservatives. It has a smooth, creamy texture, a mild flavor, and retains most of the nutrients of the original vegetable.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: NFS (Not From Concentrate) indicates the product is made from whole fresh potatoes, not from a reconstituted concentrate.
Mashed potato is a common component of infant foods because of its easy digestibility.
When stored properly, the product can maintain its quality for up to 12 months.
Potatoes are one of the most widely cultivated vegetables worldwide and mashed potato is a classic side dish.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Fresh potatoes provide vitamin C, which supports the immune system and collagen synthesis.

items.title: Good source of potassium
items.content: Potassium helps regulate fluid balance and supports normal heart function.

items.title: Contains dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber promotes healthy digestion and contributes to satiety.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Mashed potato without added butter or cream contains little saturated fat.

items.title: Contains vitamin B6
items.content: Vitamin B6 is involved in protein metabolism and neurotransmitter synthesis.

items.title: Potato allergy
items.content: A small number of individuals may experience an allergic reaction to potatoes.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: If salt is added to the finished product, intake should be monitored, especially for people with hypertension.

items.title: Bacterial growth after opening
items.content: Once the package is opened, keep the product refrigerated and consume within a few days to prevent bacterial contamination.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve as a side dish with meat, fish or vegetables, use in casseroles, soups, or infant meals. For extra flavor you can add butter, milk, or herbs and spices.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a sealed package in a cool, dry place. After opening, keep refrigerated and use within 5 days. Discard if an off‑odor or discoloration appears.

content.title: About
content.content: Shirley Temple is a non‑alcoholic cocktail named after the famous American child actress of the 1930s. It is made from ginger ale (or lemonade), grenadine and is garnished with a maraschino cherry. The drink has a bright red color and a sweet‑tart flavor, often served at children’s parties and family restaurants.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The drink first appeared in the United States in the 1930s as a “kid’s cocktail”.
It was named after Shirley Temple after the actress tried it in a café and liked it.
Traditional recipes use ginger ale, but some versions substitute lemonade or sparkling water.
Grenadine gives the characteristic red hue and a subtle fruit note.
In some countries the drink is served with a slice of pineapple or lime instead of a cherry.

items.title: Source of vitamin C
items.content: Grenadine, made from pomegranate juice, provides vitamin C which supports the immune system.

items.title: Controlled sugar content
items.content: When prepared at home you can limit added sugar, making the drink less sweet.

items.title: Hydration
items.content: The sparkling water or ginger ale helps maintain the body’s fluid balance.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Pomegranate juice is rich in antioxidants that combat free radicals.

items.title: Soothing ginger effect
items.content: Ginger ale may ease mild stomach discomfort.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Commercial versions often contain a lot of sugar, which can contribute to weight gain and tooth decay.

items.title: Pomegranate allergy
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to pomegranate, an ingredient of grenadine.

items.title: Carbonated beverages
items.content: Large amounts of carbonated drinks can cause stomach discomfort in sensitive people.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: Acidic components (lemon juice, grenadine) may irritate the mucosa if consumed excessively.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve Shirley Temple chilled in a tall glass with ice, a splash of grenadine, a maraschino cherry and, optionally, a lime wedge. For a homemade version mix ginger ale, grenadine and lemon juice in a 3:1:0.5 ratio.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the prepared drink in the refrigerator for no more than 24 hours. Keep the individual ingredients (ginger ale, grenadine) in sealed containers away from light.

content.title: About
content.content: Tomato Chili Sauce is a spicy condiment made from ripe tomatoes, chili peppers, vinegar and a blend of spices. It delivers a rich tomato flavor with moderate heat and works well as a topping for meat, fish, vegetables, and Asian-inspired dishes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Tomato chili sauce is a staple in Mexican and Thai cuisines for adding heat and depth of flavor.
The vitamin C content can provide up to 15 % of the daily value per 100 g, depending on the tomato proportion.
Chili peppers contribute capsaicin, which not only adds spiciness but also a thermogenic effect.
Traditional recipes include vinegar, which extends the product’s shelf life.
The sauce may be smooth or contain chili pieces, depending on the manufacturing process.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Tomatoes and chilies provide lycopene and vitamin E, which help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Metabolism support
items.content: Capsaicin in chilies can boost metabolism and aid calorie burning.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: The sauce contains modest amounts of B6 and folate, important for nervous system function.

items.title: Mineral content
items.content: Potassium and magnesium are present, supporting heart and muscle health.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Tomato chili sauce is typically low in fat, making it suitable for calorie‑controlled diets.

items.title: Spicy food sensitivity
items.content: High heat can cause discomfort for people with sensitive stomachs or gastritis.

items.title: Tomato allergy
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to tomatoes or the spices used in the sauce.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: The sauce often contains a notable amount of salt; those with hypertension should monitor portions.

items.title: Preservatives
items.content: Commercial versions may include preservatives that can trigger reactions in sensitive consumers.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Use tomato chili sauce as a marinade for meat, a topping for burritos, tacos, pizza, pasta, or as a dip for vegetable sticks and shrimp. It can be blended with mayo or sour cream for a milder flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the sauce in a tightly sealed jar in the refrigerator after opening. Unopened, it can be stored at room temperature for up to 12 months. Discard if you notice off‑smell, color changes, or mold growth.

content.title: About
content.content: Turkey neck is meat taken from the cervical region of the bird. It has a rich flavor, moderate fat content, and a firm texture. The neck is commonly used for braising, roasting, and making stocks.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Turkey neck contains more connective tissue, making it especially tender when cooked slowly.
In many traditional cuisines the neck is considered a delicacy and is often served at festive meals.
The meat is rich in collagen, which is beneficial for skin and joint health.
When properly marinated, the neck can acquire a flavor similar to breast meat but with a deeper, meatier note.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Turkey neck provides about 20 g of protein per 100 g, supporting muscle maintenance.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: It contains vitamins B3, B6 and B12, important for energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Rich in minerals
items.content: The neck supplies iron, zinc and phosphorus, which are essential for blood formation and bone health.

items.title: Low in carbohydrates
items.content: Like most meats, turkey neck contains virtually no carbs, making it suitable for low‑carb diets.

items.title: Poultry allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to poultry meat.

items.title: Fat content
items.content: The neck is fattier than the breast, so those monitoring fat intake should watch portion sizes.

items.title: Thorough cooking required
items.content: As with any meat, turkey neck must be cooked to a safe internal temperature to avoid food‑borne illness.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Turkey neck can be braised in sauce, roasted with herbs, cooked in a slow cooker, or used to make a flavorful broth. Marinating it in olive oil, spices and lemon juice before cooking enhances tenderness and taste.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep fresh turkey neck refrigerated at 0‑4 °C for 2‑3 days. For longer storage, freeze it in an airtight bag at ‑18 °C, where it remains good for up to 6 months. Thaw frozen neck in the refrigerator before cooking.

turkey-with-vegetable-stuffing-diet-froz.title: Turkey with vegetable, stuffing, diet frozen meal

content.title: About
content.content: Turkey with vegetable, stuffing is a ready‑to‑heat diet frozen meal containing turkey pieces, a blend of vegetables (carrot, broccoli, cauliflower) and a light whole‑grain rice stuffing with herbs. The meal is designed for quick microwave preparation and fits a controlled‑calorie diet.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Turkey is one of the leanest meats, high in protein and low in calories.
Vegetables are flash‑frozen, preserving most of their vitamins and minerals.
Diet frozen meals are often formulated to balance macronutrients: roughly 30 % calories from protein, 30 % from fat and 40 % from carbs.
The product contains no artificial colors or flavors, only natural spices.
Packaging is made from recyclable plastic, reducing environmental impact.

items.title: High protein content
items.content: Turkey provides about 20 g of protein per serving, supporting muscle maintenance.

items.title: Low calorie count
items.content: The meal is around 250 kcal, making it suitable for weight‑management plans.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: Turkey and vegetables supply B3, B6 and B12 vitamins important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Source of dietary fiber
items.content: Vegetables and whole‑grain stuffing deliver roughly 5 g of fiber, aiding digestion.

items.title: Low sodium level
items.content: The recipe uses a modest amount of salt, beneficial for blood‑pressure control.

items.title: Poultry allergy
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to bird meat and should avoid the product.

items.title: Presence of glutamate
items.content: Certain formulations may contain sodium glutamate, which can trigger headaches in sensitive people.

items.title: Must be heated to 75 °C
items.content: Insufficient heating may leave live bacteria; follow the recommended heating time.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Microwave the frozen meal according to the package directions (typically 3–4 minutes on high), stir, and let stand for 1 minute. Serve as a standalone lunch or with a light side salad.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the product frozen at –18 °C or lower. Once the package is opened and transferred to the fridge, consume within 24 hours.
